fields.meta_title: Maintenance Page Builder With Live Updates | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a maintenance page from a prompt that collects emails, posts live updates, and alerts you when a request needs a person.
fields.h1: Build a Maintenance Page for Planned Downtime
fields.hero_description: Get a maintenance page that takes emails and requests while you work, and saves each one to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts of a Maintenance Page That Works
fields.features_subheading: Visitors see one screen and a return time. Behind it, Emergent keeps the people who are waiting and the requests they leave.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt for the page and its form

Describe the work, the window, and what visitors can do while they wait. Emergent builds the page with its form and the table behind it, and changes any line when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
A notify list in a database you own

Every email left on the page becomes a row in a database you own, with the time it arrived. When the site is back, the whole list gets one message, sent by email from the app.
fields.feature_3:
Status lines that appear as you post them

Post a new line from the dashboard and it shows on the page without anyone reloading. Earlier lines stay in view for the visitor who arrives late and wants to know what changed.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts for requests that need a person

Set the rule for what cannot wait, such as a large booking or a message marked urgent. That request goes to Slack or to the person on call by email. The rest wait in the table.
fields.feature_5:
A subdomain apart from the main server

Publish the page on a custom domain, which is included and uses credits. Give it a subdomain such as status.yourstore.com that does not run on the server you are taking down.
fields.feature_6:
Free to start, with the code yours later

The free tier covers building and publishing the page. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository, ready to serve from your own stack the next time.

fields.tab_content_1:
318 shoppers got one email when the store came back

Thessaly Home, a home goods shop, took its store offline on Sunday from 2 AM to 6 AM for a platform upgrade. Its maintenance page gave the return time and asked for an email. By 6 AM, 318 shoppers had left one, Imelda Trask among them. When the store reopened, each got one email with a free shipping code.
fields.tab_content_2:
The finish time moved to 1:30 AM, and the page said so

Quarrytask, a project tracking app, moved its database to a new server, with the work set for 11 PM to 1 AM. Engineer Ottilie Brandt posted each update to the maintenance page, and visitors saw it appear without reloading. At 12:40 AM, her third update moved the finish time to 1:30 AM. The app was back at 1:24 AM.
fields.tab_content_3:
Tables for 6 or more go to the manager on Slack

For 2 days, Pennywort Bistro switched booking systems, and its maintenance page took table requests. It saved 42 requests. Any request for 6 or more guests sent manager Delphine Ashby a Slack message. Ambrose Penhallow asked for a table for 8 on Friday at 7 PM.
fields.tab_content_4:
A live count showed 540 of 1,260 visitors came to renew

Brightmoor Public Library moved its online catalog over 3 days. Its maintenance page asked visitors what they came for, and a live dashboard counted the answers. Of 1,260 visitors, 540 came to renew, 410 to place a hold, and 310 for events. Branch manager Rosalind Fairweather put the renewal phone number first.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Maintenance Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to publish a maintenance page that tells visitors when you are back and takes their emails meanwhile.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the window from your own traffic
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose one thing visitors can do
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Paste it all into one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Open your analytics and find the hour with the fewest visits in a normal week. Plan the work for that hour, and tell everyone who answers customers before you set the date.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write one line on what is changing and one with the return time, such as 6 AM Eastern. Put the time in the headline, where visitors look first, and keep the reason to a sentence.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick one action: leave an email, send a request, or say what they came for. Keep it to that one form, and the page fits on a single phone screen without scrolling.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the window, the message, and the form into one prompt. Emergent returns a working draft you can open and use. Prompt again for the screen a visitor sees after they submit.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the email account that sends the back-online note, then Slack for the requests that need a person. Name the person who gets each alert, not a channel nobody reads at 2 AM.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Open the page on a phone, leave a test email, and send one request that should trigger an alert. Check that both rows sit in the table and that the alert reached the right person.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page on its own subdomain, then send visitors from the main site to it when the work starts. When the site is back, email the list and switch traffic back.

faq_plan.q: What is a maintenance page on a website?
faq_plan.ref: What is a maintenance page on a website?

prov.original: What is a maintenance page on a website?

faq_plan.a: A maintenance page is the page visitors see in place of a website while it is offline for planned work or a repair. It says what is happening and when the site will be back. A useful one also gives people something to do, such as leaving an email for a note when the site reopens.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a maintenance page?
faq_plan.a: Describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder in a few sentences: the work, the return time, and what visitors can leave while they wait. Read the first version on a phone, the way a visitor would. Then publish it on its own subdomain a day before the work starts.

faq_plan.q: How do I show a maintenance page when the server is down?
faq_plan.ref: how to show maintenance page when server is down
faq_plan.a: Serve the page from somewhere other than the server you are working on, because a server that is off cannot send any page. RFC 9110, the HTTP standard, defines the 503 status for a server that is unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance. The same standard says the server may send a Retry-After header with it.

faq_plan.q: Can I edit a maintenance page after it goes live?
faq_plan.ref: can i edit maintenance page storenvy
faq_plan.a: Yes. In Emergent, you change a live page by prompting: a new return time or a reworded line takes one sentence and a publish. Keep the page to one screen as you edit. Once it grows sections, prices, and a gallery, it has turned into a one page website.

faq_plan.q: How can I access my maintenance page while the site is down?
faq_plan.ref: how can i access my maintenance page for my airport
faq_plan.a: Open it at its own address, such as status.yourdomain.com, on a host apart from the main server. Set that address up before the work starts and bookmark it on every device you might post updates from. With Emergent, custom domains are included and use credits.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up a routine maintenance page for weekly work?
faq_plan.ref: how do i get to the brother routine maintenance page
faq_plan.a: Build it once with a fixed window, such as every Tuesday from 1 AM to 2 AM, and print that window on the page itself. A visitor who lands there then knows the outage is planned and when it ends. Each week, change only the date line.

faq_plan.q: How do I take down a maintenance page when the work ends?
faq_plan.ref: how to access brother printer's maintenance page
faq_plan.a: Switch traffic back to the main site first, then load the site yourself to confirm it is up. Keep the maintenance page's address live and change its text to say the site is back, with a link home. Deleting it would send anyone with a saved link to a 404 page.

faq_plan.q: How long should a maintenance page stay up?
faq_plan.ref: how to avoid a sight down for maintenance page
faq_plan.a: Only as long as the work, plus a margin you state on the page. Google's guide to pausing a site says that if you need to urgently disable the site for 1 to 2 days, return an informational error page with a 503 status code. It calls disabling a whole site an extreme measure for a few days at most.

faq_plan.q: How do I avoid taking a site down for a maintenance page?
faq_plan.ref: how to avoid a site down for maintenance page
faq_plan.a: Release the change to a second copy of the site and test it there. Switch traffic over once it passes. Visitors never meet a maintenance page that way. Keep the old copy running for a day in case you need to switch back.

faq_plan.q: What should a maintenance page say?
faq_plan.ref: how to change maintenance page prestashop
faq_plan.a: It should say what is changing, the hour you expect to return, and how to reach someone before then. Google Search Central's guidance on disabling a site suggests showing the date when you expect the website to be online again. If the work is a price change, say so and link the new pricing page once it is live.

plan.angle: The top 10 for maintenance page is example galleries (Atlassian, UptimeRobot, Smashing, Dribbble, Pinterest), CDN and platform setup docs (Cloudflare, Akamai, Power Pages), one HTML gist and a Reddit thread. They show what the page looks like or how to switch it on; none shows a maintenance page that does something while the site is down. This page shows four that do: a notify list that gets one email at reopening, live status updates with a moved finish time, table requests with a Slack alert, and a dashboard of what visitors came for. The FAQ covers the definition, the 503 status and Retry-After header, editing, reaching the page, routine windows, taking it down and what to say. The 404 page, one page website and pricing page are siblings: linked, never headings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Maintenance Page for Planned Downtime', title 'Maintenance Page Builder With Live Updates | Emergent' and hero 'Get a maintenance page that takes emails and requests while you work, and saves each one to a database you own.' (111 chars) cover the whole job; how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars that says what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is example galleries (Atlassian, UptimeRobot, Smashing) plus setup docs (Cloudflare, Akamai, Power Pages). Page gives 'Four Maintenance Page Examples', a seven-step how-to, and FAQ on serving the page off the main server, the 503 status and Retry-After (RFC 9110) and Google's 1 to 2 day 503 guidance.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'Pick the window from your own traffic', 'status.yourstore.com that does not run on the server you are taking down', 'Name the person who gets each alert, not a channel nobody reads at 2 AM'. Table generated from the library (QC V2/V3 clean).

openers.evidence: Every feature body and step opens on a full sentence with a verb: 'Describe the work, the window...', 'Every email left on the page becomes a row...', 'Open your analytics and find the hour...'. QC Q1 clean.

craft.evidence: No blocking craft class exists; sentences are short and varied ('The rest wait in the table.'). QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean. Repeated subdomain idea logged as a note.

voice.evidence: Calm, specific operator voice with unglamorous detail: 'her third update moved the finish time to 1:30 AM. The app was back at 1:24 AM.' No AI-tell vocabulary (QC clean). Two link-carrying FAQ sentences logged as a voice note.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, realtime, custom-domain, free-start, code-export), all in rules/capabilities.json. Third-party facts match domain_sources quotes: RFC 9110 503 'temporary overload or scheduled maintenance' and 'MAY send a Retry-After'; Google 'urgently disable the site for 1-2 days... 503', 'extreme measure... a few days at most', 'date when you expect the website to be online again'. Tab numbers agree: 540+410+310=1,260; 11 PM to 1 AM, update at 12:40 AM to 1:30 AM, back 1:24 AM.

distinct.evidence: plan-check 0 warnings; no sibling primary (404 page, one page website, pricing page) used as a heading, only as FAQ link anchors; no coming soon / waitlist / splash wording.

faq.evidence: Exactly 10 on-topic questions, none naming a brand or a file format; item 1 'What is a maintenance page on a website?' answered first sentence; hub link in item 2; sibling links one page website, 404 page, pricing page; verbatim Q1 ok; Emergent named in items 4 and 5 only (F9).

images.evidence: Contact sheet: each tab draws its copy's names and numbers (318 / Imelda Trask / Free shipping; Ottilie Brandt, 12:40 AM, Finish 1:30 AM, Back at 1:24 AM; Ambrose Penhallow, Table for 8, Friday 7 PM, Slack message to Delphine Ashby, 42 requests; 540/410/310, 1,260, Rosalind Fairweather). One hero per tab, text readable, alert to a named person. Missing Events button in tab 4 logged as image-polish note.
